subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical Windows gateway-down umbrella while maintainers split separate fixes for lifecycle, invalid-config repair, Browser plugin isolation, pricing readiness, and Claude CLI shim behavior?
rationale: The report combines credible failures across stable gateway runtime, config repair, browser runtime, provider pricing, and Windows process execution, so the fix order and product recovery surface require maintainer ownership rather than one autonomous patch.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned repairs for each proven sub-boundary.

options.title: Require live Windows proof first
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures Windows process, listener, browser, and startup timing proof for the highest-risk paths.

options.title: Close fixed sub-branches later
options.body: After proving main-only hardening ships, close or mark only the resolved Claude CLI, restart, or pricing portions while leaving remaining failures tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned repairs for each proven sub-boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-history signal across the gateway lifecycle, Windows restart, pricing, browser launch, and Windows spawn surfaces touched by the report.
